bug_description.normalized: The staged `poc` is a 65564-byte serialized SPIX image whose header words decode to `w = 25`, `h = 16384`, `d = 1`, `ncolors = 0`, and `imdata_size = 65536`, so each raster row occupies one 32-bit word and ends with 7 pad bits. `finditalic_fuzzer` passes that parsed SPIX image into `pixItalicWords()` with `debugflag = 1`, enabling the debug path that builds `pixa1` and exports it with `pixaConvertToPdf(..., L_FLATE_ENCODE, ...)`. Source inspection excludes two binary debug pages as the producer of the uninitialized bytes: the original `pixs` copy inherits fully defined raster bytes from the `memcpy()` in `pixDeserializeFromMemory()`, and the `pixd` copy inherits pad bits cleared by `pixSeedfillBinary()`. The staged artifacts do not isolate which remaining derived 1 bpp debug page first carried undefined pad bits, but they do close the shared vulnerable export boundary reached by the crashing iteration: a sub-8bpp page is routed into `pixGenerateFlateData()`, preserved as 1 bpp, and passed to `pixGetRasterData()`. There `databpl = (w + 7) / 8 = 4`, and the vulnerable loop copies all four bytes of each 25-pixel row with `GET_DATA_BYTE()` without first calling `pixSetPadBits(pixs, 0)`, so any undefined row pad bits become part of the zlib input buffer. The reproduced MemorySanitizer crash then occurs in `slide_hash()` while deflate consumes those exported bytes. The upstream fix adds `pixSetPadBits(pixs, 0)` immediately before `rdata = pixGetData(pixs)` in `pixGetRasterData()`.

source.description: First project-side read of attacker-controlled SPIX header words. These statements materialize the 25x16384, 1 bpp image geometry that later gives each exported row a partially used final byte with 7 pad bits.
source.value_from: The staged 65564-byte `poc` begins with SPIX magic `spix` and little-endian header words `w = 25`, `h = 16384`, `d = 1`, `ncolors = 0`, followed by `imdata_size = 65536` bytes of serialized raster data.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled header values `w = 25` and `d = 1` are the vulnerability-relevant values: they keep the later PDF export on the sub-8bpp path and make each row occupy one 32-bit word whose final output byte contains only one live pixel bit and 7 pad bits.

root_cause.description: `pixGetRasterData()` exports whole bytes from sub-8bpp rows without first clearing their per-row pad bits. For 25-pixel 1 bpp rows this copies a fourth byte whose remaining 7 bits are row padding into the zlib input buffer.
root_cause.note: The fix inserts `pixSetPadBits(pixs, 0);` immediately before `rdata = pixGetData(pixs)`. Source inspection excludes the original `pixs` copy and the `pixd` copy as the producer, but the staged artifacts do not isolate which remaining derived 1 bpp debug page first supplied the undefined pad bits, so the trace anchors at this shared export boundary.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. During deflate's hash-table slide, zlib branches on poisoned state derived from the raster bytes exported by `pixGetRasterData()`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/zlib/deflate.c:219:20` with stack `slide_hash -> fill_window -> deflate_slow -> deflate -> zlibCompress -> pixGenerateFlateData`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness passes the SPIX magic check and the size/dimension consistency checks in `pixDeserializeFromMemory()`, so Leptonica accepts it as a serialized PIX and returns an image object to the italic-word path.

page_disambiguation.code: pixaAddPix(pixa1, pixs, L_COPY); ... pixaAddPix(pixa1, pixsd, L_COPY); ... pixaAddPix(pixa1, pixd, L_COPY); ... pixaAddPix(pixa1, pix1, L_INSERT);
page_disambiguation.description: Source inspection keeps the trace at the shared sub-8bpp export boundary instead of naming an exact page. `pixaAddPix(..., L_COPY)` deep-copies via `pixCopy()`/`memcpy()`, so the `pixs` page added at line 181 inherits the fully initialized bytes from `pixDeserializeFromMemory()`. `pixSeedfillBinary()` clears `pixd` pad bits before line 186 adds its copy. The staged artifacts do not establish which remaining derived 1 bpp debug page later reaches `pixGetRasterData()` with undefined pad bits.

coarse_trace.summary: Leptonica parses the attacker-controlled SPIX header and raster into a 25x16384, 1 bpp PIX whose rows have a partially used final byte.
The harness calls `pixItalicWords(..., 1)`, so the debug-only PDF export path is enabled for the parsed SPIX image.

The debug branch builds `pixa1` with mixed 1 bpp and 32 bpp pages; source inspection excludes the original-page copy and the `pixd` copy as producers, but not which remaining derived 1 bpp page becomes the crashing export.
PDF generation iterates the debug pages and routes one unresolved derived 1 bpp page through `L_FLATE_ENCODE`, preserving the binary raster layout into `pixGetRasterData()`.

For that 25-pixel-wide binary page, `pixGetRasterData()` derives 4 output bytes per row and copies all four bytes without first clearing pad bits, exporting any undefined row pad bits into the zlib input buffer.
Deflate later branches on poisoned hash state while compressing the exported raster data, matching the reproduced MemorySanitizer `slide_hash -> fill_window -> deflate_slow` crash.

fine_trace.note: Reads attacker-controlled SPIX header words and materializes the witness geometry as `w = 25`, `h = 16384`, `d = 1`, `ncolors = 0`. For a 25-pixel 1 bpp image, each row later occupies one 32-bit word and therefore has 7 pad bits.

Allocates the 25x16384, 1 bpp PIX and copies the full 65536-byte serialized raster into it, producing the original `pixs` page. At this point the raster bytes, including each row's pad region, are fully defined by attacker input.
The harness passes the parsed SPIX image into `pixItalicWords()` with literal `1` for `debugflag`, enabling the debug-only PDF export path. This is a control waypoint, not the scored source.

fine_trace.var: debugflag, pixa1, pixs, pixsd, pixd, pix1
fine_trace.note: Because `debugflag` is true, `pixItalicWords()` collects several same-size debug pages into `pixa1`: the original 1 bpp page, the derived seed page, the derived italic-mask page, a later derived 1 bpp page at line 195, and two 32 bpp outline pages. Source inspection excludes the original-page copy as a producer because step 2 defined its full raster and `L_COPY` preserves those bytes, and excludes the `pixd` copy because `pixSeedfillBinary()` clears its pad bits before insertion; the staged artifacts do not isolate which remaining derived 1 bpp page later reaches export with undefined pad bits.
Requests PDF export for the debug `PIXA` and forces `L_FLATE_ENCODE`, so every page in `pixa1` is routed into the flate-compression path.

The exporter walks `pixa1` page by page. On the crashing iteration it clones one of the remaining derived 1 bpp pages from step 4, assigns `pagetype = L_FLATE_ENCODE`, and passes that exact page into `pixConvertToPdfData()`. The staged artifacts do not reveal the loop index.
Because `pagetype` is `L_FLATE_ENCODE`, `pixGenerateCIData()` routes the crash-relevant page into `pixGenerateFlateData()` instead of JPEG, JP2K, or G4 encoding.

The crash-relevant iteration stays on a 1 bpp page here: the remaining unresolved candidates from step 4 are the derived 1 bpp pages, and only that branch preserves the binary raster layout that reaches the later pad-byte export. `pixGenerateFlateData()` therefore takes the final `else` branch and clones the page unchanged, preserving the 25x16384 binary raster layout and its partially used final byte.
For a 25-pixel 1 bpp page, export derives `databpl = (25 + 7) / 8 = 4`, so each output row is packed into four whole bytes even though the fourth byte contains only one live pixel bit and 7 pad bits.

Root cause. In the `d <= 8` branch, `pixGetRasterData()` copies all four bytes of each row from the current binary raster into the packed buffer without clearing row pad bits first. Any undefined bits remaining in the fourth byte therefore become part of the exported zlib input. The fix inserts `pixSetPadBits(pixs, 0)` immediately before `rdata = pixGetData(pixs)`.

The packed raster buffer from step 10 is compressed by zlib. For any of the unresolved 25x16384, 1 bpp candidate pages, `nbytes = databpl * h = 4 * 16384 = 65536`, so any undefined pad bits copied in step 10 now enter deflate.

Sink. During `deflate_slow -> fill_window -> slide_hash`, zlib branches on poisoned hash-chain state after consuming the exported page bytes from step 11, and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this comparison-and-store.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: No. MSan's heap-origin stack points at zlib's internal `zcalloc()` buffer because the poisoned raster bytes have already entered deflate by then; the source-level root cause is Leptonica's missing `pixSetPadBits(pixs, 0)` before exporting sub-8bpp rows.

format.name: spix
format.contract: A valid 65564-byte Leptonica `spix` serialization whose header words are `w = 25`, `h = 16384`, `d = 1`, `ncolors = 0`, and `imdata_size = 65536`. Under `finditalic_fuzzer`, that image must reach `pixItalicWords(..., debugflag = 1)` so the debug PDF path exports a sub-8bpp page through `pixGetRasterData()` and zlib flate compression.
